solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 'Well done' sirloin-cut I rejected: Aga not working!

indicators.note: 'not working' reads as a broken cooker, but 'working' alone tells us to rework the letters before it
something rejected is thrown out, so the letter I is taken away from the cut of beef

parts.note: taken as written, the two words of the hyphenated cut
taken as written; an Aga is a large British range cooker
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef serves a steak with a sarcastic 'well done' because the Aga cooker has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' takes one I out of SIRLOINCUT; the rest plus AGA and NOT is rearranged, signalled by 'working', with 'not' doing double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the usual exclamation of praise offered to someone on an achievement.

clue.text: Will's endorsement brings Richard mostly into loop

indicators.note: brings ... into: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a coil is a loop of rope or wire

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Dick is the familiar form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: A legal note on someone's testament involving a man called Richard and a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement added to a testament, amending or endorsing it, is the legal term for this.

clue.text: Moneybags — initially not having a shilling

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: bob is old British slang for a shilling, a pre-decimal coin worth 12 pence

explanation.surface: A rich person who started out without a shilling to his name.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a British coin worth a twentieth of a pound, nicknamed a bob.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a very wealthy person, originally a nabob being a rich returnee from India.

clue.text: Harmonise timeless electronic composition

indicators.note: a composition is something made up or arranged, so the remaining letters are put together anew
time is abbreviated T, so being timeless means losing that letter

explanation.surface: A description of an ageless piece of electronic music that blends together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T from ELECTRONIC, leaving ELECRONIC to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring opposing views or accounts into agreement is to make them consistent with each other.

clue.text: Opportunity to improve when on the rocks?

definitions.text: Opportunity to improve when on the rocks?

parts.words: Opportunity to improve when on the rocks?
parts.note: 'on the rocks' suggests ruin, but literally a climber on a rock face needs a small grip for the foot to progress

explanation.surface: Advice that a failing marriage or business still has a chance to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' usually means in trouble; here it is a climber literally on a crag, needing a small grip for the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small initial foothold, figuratively a modest position from which further progress can be made.

clue.text: 'The Go-Between': Losey's first with Italian oddly used to bracket central episodes

indicators.note: Losey's first means the opening letter of the director's name
to bracket something is to enclose it on both sides, so one piece goes around the other
oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word
central picks the two letters in the very middle of the word

explanation.surface: Joseph Losey directed the film The Go-Between; the clue pretends to describe its making with Italian help and middle episodes.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'used' is only a link. The quoted film title doubles as the definition, since the film's title role is an intermediary.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary who carries messages between two parties, keeping communications open, is a go-between.

clue.text: Step quietly on the bus

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a tram is a public-transport vehicle like a bus, running on rails
p (piano) is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: An instruction to tread softly when boarding the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily, so a heavy step or trudge fits the verb.

clue.text: Hugo's ending gross libel with day in court

indicators.note: ending picks out the final letter of the name
gross suggests something distorted or crude, so the letters of the next words are mangled

explanation.surface: Victor Hugo's novel ends with an outrageous defamation case heard in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the familiar name of the Central Criminal Court in London, the best-known British courthouse.

clue.text: Tinsel's woven round girl's top top

indicators.note: round means one piece goes around the other
woven suggests threads interlaced, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: Tinsel's here means tinsel is, the 's being no letter

indicators.note: top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl's top made with glittering tinsel woven into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges TINSEL; 'round' wraps it about G, the first letter of 'girl's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest is a garment worn on the upper body, so it is a kind of top.

clue.text: Girl coming out to Norfolk village in break-up …

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman coming out into society
Acle is a village in Norfolk, eastern England

explanation.surface: A debutante's arrival in a Norfolk village ends in a messy split.
explanation.walkthrough: Acle is a village on the Norfolk Broads in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete collapse or fiasco, the sudden falling apart of a situation.

clue.text: … wearing one of 27? That's recklessness

parts.note: a is the indefinite article meaning one
27 across names rings given at a betrothal; a plain ring of that kind is called a band
on means wearing, as in having a coat on

explanation.surface: Wearing a betrothal ring, the clue asks, is that rashness?
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with wild abandon means acting without restraint, so the noun is a synonym of rashness.

clue.text: Caught out in breach of ASBO by C-in-C, they do naval service

indicators.note: being in breach of an order means breaking it, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: taken as written; an ASBO is a British anti-social behaviour order
taken as written

indicators.note: out means the letter for caught is removed from the commander's abbreviation

parts.note: C-in-C abbreviates commander-in-chief, taken as its letters
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A commander-in-chief catches some sailors breaking their anti-social behaviour order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C (caught) from CINC; 'in breach of' rearranges ASBO + BY + the rest. An ASBO was a British court order against nuisance behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Young lads serving officers aboard a ship are a ship's junior servants, doing naval duty.

clue.text: Fine example of cyclopaedia pupil's brought in for school

indicators.note: brought in for means one letter replaces another, the learner taking the place of school

parts.note: Pears' Cyclopaedia is a long-running British one-volume reference book
l stands for learner, a pupil

explanation.surface: A schoolchild contributes a prize entry to an encyclopaedia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in for' swaps the learner's L in place of S (school) in PEARS, from Pears' Cyclopaedia, a British reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A prized gem from an oyster is used figuratively for anything that is a superb specimen.

clue.text: Pressed lots of buttons, but ineffectually — electricity's down, for starters

indicators.note: for starters means taking the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Someone jabs at many buttons to no effect because there is a power cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobbying is urging or pressing a person, typically a politician, to support a cause.

clue.text: It does what it does in Bologna, Remo — obligingly vertical here

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word placed vertically reads upwards from the clue's run of text, so the letters are turned back
in signals letters sitting inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An Italian travel scene in which something does its thing obligingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters run backwards in the text, so the word returns, exactly as the thrown object itself does.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved throwing stick comes back to the thrower, and the hidden word comes back too, reading in reverse.

clue.text: Open letter, remove last three bits of paper, and rewrite in briefer form

indicators.note: to rewrite is to recast, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
the last three bits of the word are its closing three letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming a public letter in a newspaper, cutting and redrafting it shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' takes PER (the end of 'paper') from OPENLETTER; 'rewrite' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A short folded sheet for brief messages is a small letter, a briefer form of correspondence.

clue.text: Ben Nevis, Snowdon, Scafell Pike? That's a challenge

definitions.meaning: the highest peaks of Scotland, Wales and England listed tallest first, an arrangement by height
something difficult to achieve, a demanding request

explanation.surface: Climbing the three highest British mountains is a feat of endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The three peaks are the highest in Scotland, Wales and England, given here in descending height.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an unreasonably demanding task, and literally a sequence from highest down.

clue.text: Powerful instrument donated to hospital department

parts.note: a viol is an early stringed instrument
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A strong musical instrument given to a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forceful and intense, such as a storm, is described as strong in effect.

clue.text: Nearly all of trip's on mostly barren plain

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it
nearly all of a word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a visit is a trip; the 's here is is

indicators.note: mostly means much of the word is kept, here losing its last two letters

parts.note: bleak describes a bare, barren landscape

explanation.surface: A traveller's journey across a largely desolate flat plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like the flat landscape of the surface, but it is the adjective meaning clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain to see is obvious and able to be seen.

clue.text: Smell sheep — that's a puzzle

parts.note: a tang is a sharp smell or taste
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs out a sheep and finds it baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese dissection game, where seven shapes are arranged into figures, is a classic puzzle.

clue.text: Turned out and joined in game on Saturday

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: s is a standard abbreviation for Saturday
to have played is to have taken part in a game

explanation.surface: Someone turned out for a match on Saturday and took part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' suggests appearing for a team; here it means spread outward, as feet can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Splayed feet or limbs are spread or angled outward, which is to say turned outwards.

clue.text: Might he be good at boning fish?

definitions.text: Might he be good at boning fish?

parts.words: Might he be good at boning fish?
parts.note: a medical man skilled with a knife, and also a tropical fish with sharp spines named after him

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone would be handy at filleting.
explanation.walkthrough: A medic who operates handles bones and knives; the surgeonfish is also a real fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating doctor works with scalpels and bones, and a surgeonfish is a reef species.

clue.text: 10s reward?

definitions.meaning: 10 across in the plural, as a verb: forsakes or leaves behind
as in getting one's just ..., what one deserves

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from the phrase 'just deserts', pronounced like desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: To forsake someone is to walk out on them; deserts are also what one merits as recompense.

clue.text: Bundle of feathers scattered — three missing

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: tre is three in Italian and the Scandinavian languages

explanation.surface: A bundle of feathers blown about, with three of them lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' says the letters of TRE leave the shuffled FEATHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound bundle of corn stalks or papers is a sheaf.

clue.text: Chuck 5?

definitions.meaning: to chuck is to throw or toss
5 down is an affair, a brief romance

explanation.definitionFit: To hurl something is to throw it; a short-lived romantic affair is also called this.

clue.text: Drugs company has new lorries parked outside

indicators.note: parked outside means the lorries are placed around the other piece

parts.note: artics are articulated lorries

explanation.surface: A drug-smuggling firm with new trucks parked outside its depot.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is a British term for an articulated lorry, a large truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are drugs that dull the senses, often illegal ones.

clue.text: Writer sadly begins to lose force

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled
to lose means a letter is taken away

parts.note: g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: An author who, unfortunately, starts to lose his strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' removes G from BEGINS, leaving BEINS for 'sadly' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian dramatist of A Doll's House, is a famous playwright.

clue.text: Metalworker's fireplace

definitions.meaning: a craftsman who works in brass
a portable metal stand for burning coals

explanation.surface: A smith's hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a brass-worker and an open container burning coal for heat.

clue.text: Customer who smokes others' fags?

definitions.meaning: a consumer who finally uses a product
fags is British slang for cigarettes; someone smoking discarded stubs uses the leftovers

explanation.walkthrough: Fag is British slang for a cigarette, and a fag end is its stub.
explanation.definitionFit: The final consumer of a product; jokingly, a person who smokes the butts others leave.

clue.text: Indications of busy line in jewellery?

definitions.meaning: the occupied tone heard on a phone, sounding when the line is taken
betrothal rings worn on the finger

explanation.definitionFit: Signals that a phone is in use are tones of being occupied; the same words name betrothal rings.
